items.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. items.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. items.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, enabling bidirectional context modeling and parallel token refinement. items.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
items.summary: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. items.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
items.summary: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. items.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
items.summary: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps. First, standard benchmarks fix the number of speakers at two and ignore the near-/far-field interference, reverberation, and sudden noise of real scenes. items.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. items.summary: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. items.summary: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. items.summary: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. items.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
items.summary: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). items.summary: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. items.summary: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. items.summary: High-resolution video matting requires preserving fine details, such as hair strands and soft transparency, while maintaining consistency across frames. items.summary: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. items.summary: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) are increasingly expected to assist users while observing continuous audiovisual streams. items.summary: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality.
